objects.description: Mutable byte buffer used by the WSON serialization API to build and parse WSON-encoded data. It owns a data pointer and tracks the current read/write position and total length. Construction and destruction are managed via wson_buffer_new, wson_buffer_from, and wson_buffer_free. The buffer is advanced as values are pushed/read; callers must ensure capacity using helper functions before writing.

Alias for a UTF-16 string container implemented as std::basic_string<uint16_t>. Useful for handling UTF-16 data when working with WSON. Memory is managed by the C++ standard library; construction is the same as std::basic_string<uint16_t>.

C++ helper class that wraps the C WSON API to parse WSON-encoded data. It holds an internal wson_buffer and provides typed navigation, conversion to UTF-8 strings, number and boolean extraction, skipping values, state save/restore, and JSON conversion. Lifetimes: constructed from raw data in its constructors; destructor is expected to release any allocated buffers. Methods rely on wson.h functions for low-level parsing.

functions.name: wson_buffer_new
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a new, empty wson_buffer suitable for subsequent push/parse operations.
requirements: Must be paired with wson_buffer_free to avoid memory leaks.

functions.name: wson_buffer_require
functions.description: Ensure the buffer has at least the specified additional capacity available for writing (may grow the buffer).
requirements: buffer must be a valid pointer returned by wson_buffer_new or wson_buffer_from.
size must be >= 0. If growth occurs, previous buffer->data may be reallocated; do not keep stale raw pointers into buffer->data across calls.

functions.name: wson_push_type_boolean
functions.description: Append a boolean value with WSON type signature (WSON_BOOLEAN_TYPE_TRUE or WSON_BOOLEAN_TYPE_FALSE) to the buffer.
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.
value should be 0 or 1 (other values are unspecified).
Buffer must have or be able to acquire sufficient capacity (use wson_buffer_require or rely on internal growth if implemented).

functions.name: wson_push_type_int
functions.description: Append a 32-bit integer value with WSON integer type signature to the buffer.
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.

functions.name: wson_push_type_long
functions.description: Append a 64-bit integer value with WSON long type signature to the buffer.
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.

functions.name: wson_push_type_double
functions.description: Append a double-precision floating-point value with WSON double type signature to the buffer.
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.

functions.name: wson_push_type_float
functions.description: Append a single-precision floating-point value with WSON float type signature to the buffer.
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.

functions.name: wson_push_type_string
functions.signature: void wson_push_type_string(wson_buffer *buffer, const void *src, int32_t length);
functions.description: Append a byte string (UTF-8/byte sequence) with WSON string type signature and length to the buffer.
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.
src must point to at least length bytes; can be null only if length == 0.
length must be >= 0.

functions.name: wson_push_type_uint8_string
functions.signature: void wson_push_type_uint8_string(wson_buffer *buffer, const uint8_t *src, int32_t length);
functions.description: Append a uint8_t string (UTF-16/other 8-bit data semantics vary) with WSON UINT8 string type signature and length to the buffer.
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.
src must point to at least length bytes; can be null only if length == 0.
length must be >= 0.
Exact encoding semantics are not documented; only the raw bytes and length are required.

functions.name: wson_push_type_null
functions.description: Append a WSON null value with WSON null type signature.
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.

functions.name: wson_push_type_map
functions.description: Begin a WSON map/object by appending the map type signature and entry count.
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.
size is the number of key-value pairs to follow; must be accurate for correct parsing.

functions.name: wson_push_type_array
functions.description: Begin a WSON array by appending the array type signature and element count.
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.
size is the number of array elements to follow; must be accurate for correct parsing.

functions.name: wson_push_type_extend
functions.signature: void wson_push_type_extend(wson_buffer *buffer, const void *src, int32_t length);
functions.description: Append an extended/opaque payload with the WSON extend type signature and length.
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.
src must point to at least length bytes; can be null only if length == 0.
length must be >= 0.
The interpretation of the payload is application-defined (unknown).

functions.name: wson_push_ensure_size
functions.description: Ensure the buffer has capacity for at least dataSize bytes to be written as a contiguous block.
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.
dataSize must be >= 0. May reallocate internal storage; do not hold raw pointers into buffer->data across calls.

functions.name: wson_push_type_string_length
functions.description: Append only the WSON string type and its length prefix without writing the string bytes themselves (bytes should be written separately).
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.
length must be >= 0 and must match the number of bytes subsequently written for the string payload.

functions.name: wson_push_property
functions.signature: void wson_push_property(wson_buffer *buffer, const void *src, int32_t length);
functions.description: Append a map key/property name as a string field, typically for use inside a WSON map.
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.
src must point to at least length bytes; can be null only if length == 0.
length must be >= 0.
Caller should ensure it is used in a map context and that the overall map size matches the number of pushed properties/values.

functions.name: wson_push_int
functions.description: Append a 32-bit integer to the buffer without any WSON type signature (raw payload only).
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.
Caller must manage/precede with appropriate type information to keep the stream parseable.

functions.name: wson_push_uint
functions.description: Append a 32-bit unsigned integer to the buffer without any WSON type signature (raw payload only).
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.
Caller must manage/precede with appropriate type information to keep the stream parseable.

functions.name: wson_push_byte
functions.description: Append a single byte to the buffer (no type signature).
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.

functions.name: wson_push_type
functions.description: Append a single byte used as a WSON type signature.
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.
bt should be one of the defined WSON_*_TYPE constants.

functions.name: wson_push_double
functions.description: Append a double-precision value to the buffer without any WSON type signature (raw payload only).
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.
Caller must ensure the stream has or will have the correct type signature before this payload.

functions.name: wson_push_float
functions.description: Append a single-precision float to the buffer without any WSON type signature (raw payload only).
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.
Caller must ensure the stream carries the appropriate type signature.

functions.name: wson_push_ulong
functions.description: Append an unsigned 64-bit integer to the buffer without any WSON type signature (raw payload only).
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.
Caller must ensure the stream carries the appropriate type signature.

functions.name: wson_push_bytes
functions.signature: void wson_push_bytes(wson_buffer *buffer, const void *src, int32_t length);
functions.description: Append an arbitrary sequence of bytes to the buffer without any WSON type signature.
requirements: buffer must be valid and writeable.
src must point to at least length bytes; can be null only if length == 0.
length must be >= 0.

functions.name: wson_buffer_free
functions.description: Release the memory associated with a wson_buffer created by wson_buffer_new or adopting allocated storage, and invalidate it.
requirements: buffer may be null (no-op is expected; exact behavior unknown).
Buffer must not be used after free.

functions.name: wson_next_byte
functions.description: Read and return the next raw byte from the buffer, advancing position by 1.
requirements: buffer must be valid and have at least 1 remaining byte.
Position must be within [0, length).

functions.name: wson_next_type
functions.description: Read and return the next WSON type signature byte from the buffer, advancing position by 1.
requirements: buffer must be valid and have at least 1 remaining byte.
The stream should be aligned at a type boundary for correct parsing.

functions.name: wson_next_int
functions.description: Read and return the next 32-bit integer payload from the buffer (no type read), advancing position accordingly.
requirements: buffer must be valid and have enough remaining bytes for a 32-bit integer payload.
Caller must have already consumed and validated the corresponding type signature if present.

functions.name: wson_next_uint
functions.description: Read and return the next 32-bit unsigned integer payload from the buffer (no type read), advancing position accordingly.
requirements: buffer must be valid and have enough remaining bytes for a 32-bit unsigned integer payload.
Caller must have already consumed and validated the corresponding type signature if present.

functions.name: wson_next_double
functions.description: Read and return the next double-precision payload from the buffer (no type read), advancing position accordingly.
requirements: buffer must be valid and have enough remaining bytes for a double payload.
Caller must have already consumed and validated the corresponding type signature if present.

functions.name: wson_next_float
functions.description: Read and return the next single-precision float payload from the buffer (no type read), advancing position accordingly.
requirements: buffer must be valid and have enough remaining bytes for a float payload.
Caller must have already consumed and validated the corresponding type signature if present.

functions.name: wson_next_long
functions.description: Read and return the next 64-bit integer payload from the buffer (no type read), advancing position accordingly.
requirements: buffer must be valid and have enough remaining bytes for a 64-bit integer payload.
Caller must have already consumed and validated the corresponding type signature if present.

functions.name: wson_next_ulong
functions.description: Read and return the next unsigned 64-bit integer payload from the buffer (no type read), advancing position accordingly.
requirements: buffer must be valid and have enough remaining bytes for a 64-bit unsigned integer payload.
Caller must have already consumed and validated the corresponding type signature if present.

functions.name: wson_next_bts
functions.description: Return a pointer to the next length bytes in the buffer and advance position by length. Does not copy data.
requirements: buffer must be valid and have at least length remaining bytes.
length must be >= 0.
The returned pointer becomes invalid if the buffer is reallocated or freed; use or copy immediately.

functions.name: wson_has_next
functions.description: Return true if there are remaining unread bytes in the buffer (position < length).
requirements: buffer must be valid (non-null).

functions.name: wson_buffer_from
functions.description: Construct a wson_buffer view over an existing memory block of the given length, with initial position at start.
requirements: data must be non-null if length > 0.
length must be >= 0.
The lifetime of data must outlive the wson_buffer unless the implementation copies it (unknown). Avoid freeing data while the buffer is in use.

functions.name: wson_parser::wson_parser
functions.description: Construct a wson_parser from a pointer to WSON-encoded bytes. Length handling is unspecified in the header; likely parses until a terminator or embedded lengths.
requirements: data must be a valid pointer to a WSON byte sequence; must remain valid for the lifetime of the parser unless the implementation copies it.
Exact data termination/length semantics are unknown from the header.

functions.name: wson_parser::~wson_parser
functions.description: Destroy the parser and release any associated resources/buffers.
requirements: Do not use the parser after destruction.

functions.name: wson_parser::hasNext
functions.description: Return whether there are more unread bytes in the underlying buffer.
requirements: Parser must have been successfully constructed.

functions.name: wson_parser::nextType
functions.description: Return the next WSON type byte and advance the parser. Returns WSON_NULL_TYPE if no data is available.
requirements: Parser must have been successfully constructed.
Underlying buffer must contain at least one byte to read a real type.

functions.name: wson_parser::backType
functions.description: Step the parser position back by one byte to undo a previous type read.
requirements: Current position must be > 0.

functions.name: wson_parser::isMap
functions.description: Return true if the provided type byte denotes a WSON map (object).
requirements: Argument must be a previously read type byte.

functions.name: wson_parser::isArray
functions.description: Return true if the provided type byte denotes a WSON array.
requirements: Argument must be a previously read type byte.

functions.name: wson_parser::isString
functions.description: Return true if the provided type byte denotes a WSON string-like type (string, uint8 string, big int, big decimal).
requirements: Argument must be a previously read type byte.

functions.name: wson_parser::isBool
functions.description: Return true if the provided type byte denotes a WSON boolean.
requirements: Argument must be a previously read type byte.

functions.name: wson_parser::isNumber
functions.description: Return true if the provided type byte denotes a numeric WSON type (int, float, long, double).
requirements: Argument must be a previously read type byte.

functions.name: wson_parser::isNull
functions.description: Return true if the provided type byte denotes a WSON null.
requirements: Argument must be a previously read type byte.

functions.name: wson_parser::nextMapSize
functions.description: Read and return the size (entry count) of a WSON map, advancing the parser position accordingly.
requirements: The next value in the stream must be a map size field; typically call after reading a map type.

functions.name: wson_parser::nextArraySize
functions.description: Read and return the size (element count) of a WSON array, advancing the parser position accordingly.
requirements: The next value in the stream must be an array size field; typically call after reading an array type.

functions.name: wson_parser::nextMapKeyUTF8
functions.description: Read the next map key and return it as a UTF-8 std::string, performing any required decoding.
requirements: The parser should be positioned at a map key.
Underlying data must contain a valid string key in expected encoding.

functions.name: wson_parser::nextStringUTF8
functions.description: Read the next value of the specified type and return it as a UTF-8 std::string, converting from string/number representations as needed.
requirements: type should be a string-like or numeric type supported by conversion.
The stream must contain a valid payload for the provided type.

functions.name: wson_parser::nextNumber
functions.description: Read the next value of the specified type and return it as a double. If type is string, converts the string to a number.
requirements: type should denote a numeric or string type that can be converted to a number.
The stream must contain a valid payload for the provided type.

functions.name: wson_parser::nextBool
functions.description: Read the next value of the specified type and return it as a boolean.
requirements: type should denote a boolean or a type convertible to boolean per implementation.
The stream must contain a valid payload for the provided type.

functions.name: wson_parser::skipValue
functions.description: Skip over the next value of the given type without decoding it, advancing the parser position accordingly.
requirements: type must correspond to the next value in the stream.
The parser must be positioned at the beginning of that value.

functions.name: wson_parser::resetState
functions.description: Reset the parser position to the start of the buffer.
requirements: Parser must have been successfully constructed.

functions.name: wson_parser::getState
functions.description: Return the current byte position within the underlying buffer.

functions.name: wson_parser::restoreToState
functions.description: Set the parser position to a previously saved state and return the new position.
requirements: state must be within [0, buffer length].

functions.name: wson_parser::toStringUTF8
functions.description: Convert the entire WSON payload to a JSON-like UTF-8 string representation.
requirements: Underlying data must be valid WSON; behavior is undefined for malformed streams.

functions.name: wson::utf16_convert_to_utf8_string
functions.signature: void wson::utf16_convert_to_utf8_string(uint16_t *utf16, int length, char* decodingBuffer, std::string& utf8);
functions.description: Convert a UTF-16 sequence to UTF-8, using a caller-provided temporary buffer, and append/write to utf8.
requirements: utf16 must point to at least length 16-bit code units.
length must be >= 0.
decodingBuffer must be large enough to hold the converted UTF-8 (size requirement depends on input; up to ~4 bytes/code unit in worst cases).
utf8 string reference must be valid.

functions.name: wson::utf16_convert_to_utf8_quote_string
functions.signature: void wson::utf16_convert_to_utf8_quote_string(uint16_t *utf16, int length, char* decodingBuffer, std::string& utf8);
functions.description: Convert a UTF-16 sequence to a JSON-quoted and escaped UTF-8 string, using a caller-provided temporary buffer, and append/write to utf8.
requirements: utf16 must point to at least length 16-bit code units.
length must be >= 0.
decodingBuffer must be large enough for the converted and escaped UTF-8.
utf8 string reference must be valid.

functions.name: wson::utf16_convert_to_utf8_cstr
functions.signature: int wson::utf16_convert_to_utf8_cstr(uint16_t *utf16, int length, char* buffer);
functions.description: Convert a UTF-16 sequence to UTF-8 and write it into buffer as a C string. Returns the number of bytes written (likely excluding the null terminator).
requirements: utf16 must point to at least length 16-bit code units.
length must be >= 0.
buffer must be large enough to hold the converted string plus a null terminator.

functions.name: wson::utf16_convert_to_utf8_quote_cstr
functions.description: Convert a UTF-16 sequence to a JSON-quoted and escaped UTF-8 C string. Returns the number of bytes written (likely excluding the null terminator).
requirements: utf16 must point to at least length 16-bit code units.
length must be >= 0.
buffer must be large enough to hold the converted and escaped UTF-8 string plus a null terminator.

functions.name: wson::str_append_number
functions.description: Append a textual representation of a double to the supplied string.
requirements: str reference must be valid.

data_types.description: A sequence of raw bytes of any value and length. No specific encoding or structure is required (may contain binary data, UTF-8 text, or any other arbitrary content). Used when APIs accept a pointer and length to uninterpreted data or generic byte strings.
